prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Document units:
U0047: This lead time allows enough time for traffic managers to evaluate, modify, and coordinate the reroute, and for controllers to issue clearances and deconflict flights prior to the merge point.
U0048: MFCR selects an RCF waypoint that is as far downstream as typically acceptable in local Center operations and is common to the original flight plan routes for all the flights in the group.
U0049: This point represents the flight plan fix at which the flights return to their original flight plan route.
U0050: Reroutes avoid convective weather, SUAs, and TFRs scheduled to be active at the time the reroute transits the airspace.
U0051: Due to the number and variety of other constraints that may impact a direct route, the MFCR algorithm does not avoid all operational constraints, such as congested sectors, sector traversal restrictions (e.g., crossing arrival/departure sectors, proximity to sector boundaries), fix- crossing restrictions, or other restrictions imposed by letters of agreement.
U0052: The variables and complex factors associated with these types of constraints are extremely difficult to implement effectively in automation tools without imposing requirements on a multitude of other systems.
U0053: Instead, MFCR provides the user with constraint information and a user-friendly trial planning function that allows the user to tailor reroutes to fit the operational scenario.
U0054: Named fixes are used for all waypoints for ease of use where available; otherwise, waypoints are defined by fix, radial, and distance (FRD).
U0055: A snap-to named fix capability automatically replaces any auxiliary waypoints with nearby named fixes for ease of use in voice-based operations, but traffic managers may still opt to use a FRD fix.
U0056: The current flight plan trajectory and the MFCR reroute trajectories are both analyzed for sector loading and conflicts with active SUAs or TFRs.
U0057: All conflicts are displayed on the user interface, thereby providing immediate feedback to the user about the suitability of a MFCR recommended reroute or a user modification of a recommended reroute.
U0058: Recommended reroutes and all the associated data are also updated every minute with traffic updates.
U0059: Figure 2: Example of MFCR Direct Route Limit Regions The default location of the RCF is intended to approximate an operationally acceptable route clearance based on direct routes historically approved for flights in the Center.
U0060: Direct route clearance data collected for the previous one-year period are used to create “limit polygons” for each Center, as denoted by the cyan colored polygons in the example shown in Figure 2.
U0061: The three limit polygons shown in Figure 2 are for Minneapolis Center (top), Fort Worth Center (bottom-left), and Atlanta Center (bottom-right).
U0062: Each limit polygon spans multiple Centers.
U0063: MFCR will select a waypoint, common to all the flight plan routes within the group, which is on or close to the downstream boundary of the limit polygon of the Center in which the flights are currently located.
U0064: This method indirectly accounts for Center preferences and routine constraints.
U0065: A more complete set of Traffic Flow Management (TFM) and Air Traffic Control (ATC) constraints may enable use of other methods to extend the range within which RCFs may be selected.
U0066: MFCR checks downstream Time-Based Flow Management (TBFM) arrival metering constraints for each flight before including it in the recommended reroute.
U0067: The MFCR research prototype uses a simple proxy for this check, based on distance to destination.
U0068: As long as a flight is outside its destination’s TBFM planning horizon, it will be considered for inclusion in time-saving reroutes.
U0069: Future integration between MFCR and TBFM could enable the negotiation of a revised scheduled time of arrival (STA) for flights inside the TBFM planning horizon based on reroute savings and permit these flights to benefit from MFCR’s en route delay recovery.
U0070: Flights inside the TBFM freeze horizon would still be excluded from MFCR reroutes. 4.2 USER INTERFACE AND PROCEDURES MFCR reroute recommendations are presented to the appropriate TMC, who evaluates and modifies it as needed.
U0071: Figure 3 shows an example of the user interface.
U0072: The bottom left portion of the display lists recommended group reroutes, showing overall savings for the group and the number of flights in the group.
U0073: Selecting a group in this pane highlights the line in yellow and brings up a list of flights for that group in the lower right portion of the display with a breakdown of individual flight savings, the Center in which the flight is currently located, inclusion of the flight in a TMI, conflicts with congested sectors and SUA, and waypoints for each flight’s new route.
